View: The June 19, 2014 LMI ICA establishes first-versus-second lien priority on shared Collateral and a documented Company-plus-eighteen-Guarantor acknowledgment perimeter. It does not locate economic value across that perimeter. The strongest established second-lien weakness is conditional loss of independent collateral/guarantee access through first-lien-led releases and control, not a demonstrated drop-down or entity-level structural-subordination gap. Reciprocal new-lien requirements and similar-collateral intent materially protect reach, but actual equity exceptions and written elections can create class-only collateral. Consequently, neither an overall leakage severity nor a numeric recovery is supportable. Preserve all named entities and test the underlying instruments and values before converting this qualitative architecture into claims or recoveries.

Company/Guarantors must grant corresponding liens for additional 1L or 2L security before discharge; appropriate grant action without agent perfection is not a breach. Mutual no-contest stabilizes agreed rank, but 1L may enforce priority and 2L waives marshaling. This protects common reach, not perfection assurance

Identical-collateral intent is qualified: subsidiary equity excluded from 2L to extent Rule 3-16 would require otherwise-unrequired separate SEC financials, only to extent not filed; foreign-subsidiary equity may be 1L-only where a 2L pledge is prohibited/unenforceable locally, subject to the bailee/custodian/agent qualification; later new/excluded/separately-granted asset types may differ where the other agent elects in writing not to obtain its lien after prior written notice. No blanket exclusion of any named entity follows

Actual release architecture; no actual release event established

Enforcement-related 1L lien releases can trigger automatic 2L lien releases; guarantee release tied to sale of all Guarantor equity and 1L guarantee release. Ordinary dispositions require 1L permission and no express 2L prohibition. These are access-loss mechanics, not independent disposal baskets
High on text; CP-4D must test transaction conditions and proceeds
Documented controls, no enforcement trigger supplied

At least 180 days from later of 2L default declaration plus repayment demand and 1L receipt of declaration notice; at least 15 days prior written enforcement notice, which may run during standstill. Expiry does not override diligent 1L material-collateral enforcement or specified stay-relief activity. 1L controls remedies; contravening receipts and specified insolvency collateral distributions turn over before discharge. Residual proceeds remain for 2L; not a universal ordinary-payment block
High on text; CP-4D to build trigger chronology and credit-bid analysis

rows.label: F5 — amendment/refinancing asymmetry, not proved uptier

cells.text: Actual ICA permissions; no used non-pro-rata capacity proved

1L amendments/refinancing can proceed without 2L consent subject to terms and written binding of refinancing holders; refinancing can prevent discharge. Automatic comparable security amendments have asset-release, extra-duty, impermissible-lien and disproportionate-prejudice safeguards plus notice. ICA amendments require both agents, 2L acting with majority-principal Notes consent. §7.3 preserves priority despite broad 1L changes; it does not prove unlimited incurrence or intra-class uptiering authority
High on ICA; underlying sacred rights, sharing and purchase provisions missing; no Priming-Exposed/Trapdoor label
Conditional DIP subordination documented, no actual DIP proved

2L non-objection/subordination for qualifying cash collateral/DIP use is subject to aggregate principal/LC ceiling of Maximum First Lien Indebtedness Amount plus $10m. 1L-approved §363 sales have stated proceeds/cap-reduction conditions; stay relief and adequate protection constrained. Junior additional/replacement liens and admin claims permitted only on specified senior-priority terms; avoidance may reinstate priority; plan, interest, proof-of-claim and credit-bid provisions further shape access
High on text, no capacity dollars; CP-4D must consume full §6, not treat this as its completion

1L holds possessed/control collateral as bailee/non-fiduciary for stated perfection purpose, not ownership/genuineness assurance; collateral-preservation and information duties are limited. Enforcement/discharge notice failures do not waive rights or create stated liability. 2L must independently monitor value and triggers rather than rely on agent notice or custody as a completeness audit
High on text; obtain custody/control records and independent monitoring

Fact → mechanism → consequence: LMI's ICA recitals and individual acknowledgments describe multi-entity support for both classes; §§2.1 and 4.1 allocate shared collateral first to 1L, then 2L. That supports a qualitative lien-priority finding, not “structurally subordinated” notes by entity. No named non-guarantor value or stranded pool is established, and no route meets the entity-path, enabling-capacity and exposed-value test for a numeric leakage score. Overall leakage risk therefore remains Not Scorable, not a default medium score or average.

The strongest counterargument to weak 2L reach is §§2.3–2.4: reciprocal grants, good-faith cooperation and substantially matching documents resist unilateral collateral expansion. This argument would prevail economically if the underlying schedules show materially coextensive, perfected coverage, no material equity exceptions/elections and sufficient shared value after actual senior obligations. It cannot erase 1L control or conditional releases. Conversely, material excluded equity or a documented election would make collateral asymmetry economically important; entity names alone do not establish either.

Conditional downside, not a historical event claim: if a Company or mapped Guarantor default triggers 2L acceleration and notice before 1L discharge, the first legal break is loss of unilateral collateral enforcement under §3.1. Continuing operations or asset deterioration could then reduce collateral available while senior interest/fees and qualifying financing absorb proceeds. A 1L-led sale and §5.1 release could convert 2L support into a residual proceeds claim; refinancing under §5.6 can prolong senior priority. This is primarily an access/LGD and refinancing-control mechanism, not proof of increased PD or any recovery percentage. Observable tests are default/demand and received-notice dates, diligent enforcement/stay applications, proposed sale/release terms, actual claims, collateral valuations and DIP orders. No operational deterioration or default is established by this source.

Confidence is high for cited ICA mechanics, limited for independent entity support and insufficient for economic ranking/capacity. No computed confidence score or native acceptance is claimed: the supplied tools do not provide the selected method's confidence script. This does not change the explicit scope limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: View: The June 19, 2014 LMI ICA establishes first-versus-second lien priority on shared Collateral and a documented Company-plus-eighteen-Guarantor acknowledgment perimeter. It does not locate economic value across that perimeter. The strongest established second-lien weakness is conditional loss of independent collateral/guarantee access through first-lien-led releases and control, not a demonstrated drop-down or entity-level structural-subordination gap. Reciprocal new-lien requirements and similar-collateral intent materially protect reach, but actual equity exceptions and written elections can create class-only collateral. Consequently, neither an overall leakage severity nor a numeric recovery is supportable. Preserve all named entities and test the underlying instruments and values before converting this qualitative architecture into claims or recoveries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This single lossless matrix explicitly serves **T4D.2 perimeter, T4D.3 guarantee, T4D.4 security and T4D.5 entity-priority views**. These are individual source-order acknowledgers, not a complete group. All financial dashes mean **Not supplied: entity assets, EBITDA and carrying debt are undisclosed**, not zero. Ownership percentages, operating/holding-company roles, guarantee direction, caps and local-law limitations are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Common reference **P** = ICA p.1 recitals L11–L16; p.1 §1.1 Credit Parties L59; p.2 Guarantors L109; p.11 acknowledgment L588–L591. P describes Company borrowings/issuance, Guarantor support and substantially all personal-property security under underlying documents. It is not an independently examined guarantee/security grant. Common reference **Q** = ICA pp.3–4 §§2.1–2.4 L183–L212; pp.5–6 §5.1 L270–L282: first/second lien rank on shared Collateral, equity/election qualifications and conditional releases. No row is assigned an exception merely from its name. “Structural rank unproved” means insufficient information to rank reachable value by entity or name stranded value, not an adverse finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Fact → mechanism → consequence:** LMI's ICA recitals and individual acknowledgments describe multi-entity support for both classes; §§2.1 and 4.1 allocate shared collateral first to 1L, then 2L. That supports a qualitative lien-priority finding, not “structurally subordinated” notes by entity. No named non-guarantor value or stranded pool is established, and no route meets the entity-path, enabling-capacity and exposed-value test for a numeric leakage score. Overall leakage risk therefore remains **Not Scorable**, not a default medium score or average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest counterargument to weak 2L reach is §§2.3–2.4: reciprocal grants, good-faith cooperation and substantially matching documents resist unilateral collateral expansion. This argument would prevail economically if the underlying schedules show materially coextensive, perfected coverage, no material equity exceptions/elections and sufficient shared value after actual senior obligations. It cannot erase 1L control or conditional releases. Conversely, material excluded equity or a documented election would make collateral asymmetry economically important; entity names alone do not establish either.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Conditional downside, not a historical event claim:** if a Company or mapped Guarantor default triggers 2L acceleration and notice before 1L discharge, the first legal break is loss of unilateral collateral enforcement under §3.1. Continuing operations or asset deterioration could then reduce collateral available while senior interest/fees and qualifying financing absorb proceeds. A 1L-led sale and §5.1 release could convert 2L support into a residual proceeds claim; refinancing under §5.6 can prolong senior priority. This is primarily an access/LGD and refinancing-control mechanism, not proof of increased PD or any recovery percentage. Observable tests are default/demand and received-notice dates, diligent enforcement/stay applications, proposed sale/release terms, actual claims, collateral valuations and DIP orders. No operational deterioration or default is established by this source.

No computed confidence score or native acceptance is claimed: the supplied tools do not provide the selected method's confidence script. This does not change the explicit scope limitations.
